THE RATIO IS NOW COMPUTED AND IT DOES NOT MEET THE TARGET. Target: spoor enabled adds <= 2% p99 and <= 2% CPU cycles; allocations = 0; torn records = 0. MEASURED ON SILICON 2026-08-06, BOTH ARMS IN ONE BOOT (Raspberry Pi 5, Tier 1, kernel8.img sha256 05f3495c3352176f01b7ae3f2a06ec1dd42f0a7efd488e8bb551fce25454e085, envelope harvested off the wire and parsed by the UNCHANGED xtask parser, metrics=12): pool_u64x64_alloc_free_round_trip_per_op_of_8 p99 = 479 cycles/op with spoor DISABLED, and the byte-identical loop plus one stamp per round trip p99 = 604 cycles/op ENABLED. Delta 125 cycles/op = +26.1 percent against a 2 percent allowance. THIS IS A FAIL BY MORE THAN 13x AND IS RECORDED AS ONE. Two clauses do hold: allocations = 0 is compiler-enforced, and torn records = 0 was observed across 160+ records at 0 refused 0 lost with the sequence unbroken. READ THE DENSITY BEFORE QUOTING THE 26 PERCENT: the enabled arm stamps ONCE PER POOL OPERATION, the deliberate worst case and not a realistic instrumentation density, so the figure over-states overhead rather than flattering it. The useful derived result is what the gate actually constrains: 2 percent of 479 cycles is 9.6 cycles and a stamp costs 137 (p50, same boot), so the budget admits ONE STAMP PER ~14 POOL OPERATIONS. G23 is a constraint on instrumentation DENSITY, not on stamp cost, and nothing in this project had said so because until 2026-08-06 no percentage could be computed at all -- every spoor cost on record was absolute, which is 09A section 5's finding. Both arms in ONE boot deliberately: BOARD VERDICT 9 measured ~3 percent build-to-build movement on untouched code paths, larger than the 2 percent allowance, so a pair from two runs could not answer the question AND THE SHIPPING DENSITY IS NOW COUNTED RATHER THAN GUESSED (2026-08-06, by reading the park loop, no board needed). The budget above admits one stamp per ~14 pool operations; what the shipping park loop actually does is stamp about FIVE TIMES PER SECOND. hal_arm64::ethernet's loop waits 100 ms per tick and runs the stamping body only on every tenth tick, so the beat is 1 Hz, and one beat stamps ParkIteration, ThermalSample, BeaconTransmitted when beaconing, and at most two more inside tinyos_dispatch_round -- about five stamps of 137 cycles, so ~685 cycles per second on a 2.4 GHz core, under one part in three million of CPU time. THE BEAT ALSO CONTAINS NO POOL TRAFFIC AT ALL, so the ratio this gate measures has no denominator in the shipping path: the 26.1 percent is a property of the fixture's deliberate one-stamp-per-operation arm and not of any code that ships. That does not soften the fail -- the gate asks what instrumentation costs when it is dense and the answer is 26 percent -- but it fixes what the number is FOR: it is a budget for whoever next puts a stamp inside a hot loop (14 operations per stamp), not a description of today's overhead, which is four orders of magnitude below it. Nothing here is a new measurement; it is the same 137-cycle stamp read against a density counted from the source

THE SPOOR SUBSTRATE MISSES ITS OWN MEDIAN-LATENCY GATE BY 1.9x, AND THIS IS THE FIRST TIME ANYONE READ IT AGAINST THIS TARGET. Target: p50 <= 0.03 us. Measured on silicon 2026-08-06 (Raspberry Pi 5, Tier 1, kernel8.img sha256 05f3495c3352176f01b7ae3f2a06ec1dd42f0a7efd488e8bb551fce25454e085, envelope off the wire, parsed by the unchanged xtask parser at metrics=12): spoor_stamp_park_rung_per_op_of_8 p50 = 137 cycles at cycles_per_us=2400, which is 0.0571 us. THAT IS 1.90x THE TARGET AND IS RECORDED AS THE FAIL IT IS. The number is not new -- 136 to 137 cycles has been on the wire since 2026-08-05 -- what is new is that it is labelled D11 rather than D07 and therefore read against D11's targets at last. The metric carried a D07 label because STORY-P1-10-02's contract selected only D07, so it was never compared to the gate whose subject it is; see the same Story's contract row and fixture_measure_arm64.rs. Method, stated because the verdict depends on it: the timed region is SpoorStream::stamp alone with no drain and no wire in it, the certificate is closed by an untimed first stamp so the once-per-boot retain path is not measured, eight stamps are timed per sample and divided out (SPOOR_STAMP_BATCH, LE-24), and the cycle source's calibrated overhead (43 cycles) is subtracted from the region before the division -- so at most 5 cycles of residue can be in the figure and removing every one of it still fails by 1.8x. n=1000 dropped=0 warmup=100, min 131 max 144, so the distribution is tight and the fail is not a tail artefact

NOT EVIDENCE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED. This row records that the gate was measured, read against its target, and DECLINED because the margin is inside the measurement's own noise. Target: p99 <= 0.06 us. Measured 2026-08-06 on the same boot as PERF-D11-G01: spoor_stamp_park_rung_per_op_of_8 p99 = 143 cycles at cycles_per_us=2400 = 0.0596 us, which is UNDER the target BY 0.7 PERCENT. BOARD VERDICT 9 measured ~3 percent build-to-build movement on untouched code paths, so a 0.7 percent margin is a quarter of the movement this bench has already observed from a recompile that changed nothing: the same envelope's neighbour runs put this metric's p99 at 141 (2026-08-05) and 142 (the earlier 08-05 capture), and 142 would still pass while a run 3 percent slower would not. A verdict that flips on a rebuild is not a verdict. This is PERF-D03-G20's situation exactly -- measured, read, declined -- and it is filed rather than left in prose so that no later session re-measures it from scratch or files the pass. What would settle it: a repeated-boot campaign giving a run-to-run p99 CV for this metric, at which point the gate is decidable in whichever direction the data lands; the p50 gate above needs no such campaign because 1.9x is outside any noise this bench has shown

The one of D11's three latency gates that is met with room to spare. Target: p99.9 <= 0.1 us. Measured on silicon 2026-08-06, same metric and same boot as G01 and G02: spoor_stamp_park_rung_per_op_of_8 p99_9 = 144 cycles at cycles_per_us=2400 = 0.0600 us, 40 percent under the target and 39 percent clear of the ~3 percent build-to-build movement BOARD VERDICT 9 measured -- so unlike G02 this verdict survives a rebuild and is filed as a pass rather than refused. Read the three gates together rather than separately: the distribution is extremely tight (min 131, p50 137, p99 143, p99_9 144, max 144, n=1000 dropped=0), so the substrate's problem is not its tail, it is its median. A tail gate passing while the median gate fails by 1.9x says the stamp is consistently expensive rather than occasionally so, which is the more tractable of the two shapes: there is no rare path to hunt, only a hot path to make cheaper
